requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured as the DNS resolver for the shared private network, answering inventory.internal with node2's address on that network
requirements.summary: node1's service dns forwarding was set with listen-address 10.100.11.10, allow-from 10.100.11.0/24, and authoritative-domain inventory.internal record A @ -> 10.100.11.11 (node2's private IP), committed and saved. pdns_recursor confirmed listening on 10.100.11.10:53 and dig from node1 resolved inventory.internal to 10.100.11.11.

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards all other (non-inventory.internal) DNS queries upstream
requirements.summary: name-server entries 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 were configured; dig @10.100.11.10 google.com returned real public IPs both immediately after configuration and after node1's restart, confirming forwarding works.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to resolve through node1
requirements.summary: nmcli was used on both node2 and node3 to set ipv4.dns=10.100.11.10 and ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes; resolv.conf on both nodes showed nameserver 10.100.11.10, and getent hosts on both nodes resolved inventory.internal (to 10.100.11.11) and google.com, confirming end-to-end resolution through node1.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated on node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: For each node, a pre-restart boot_id and healthy-state baseline (pdns-recursor active on node1; resolv.conf/getent working on node2/node3) was captured, a reboot was acknowledged, connectivity was polled until restored, a distinct post-restart boot_id was observed, and DNS service/resolution was re-verified as healthy post-restart on all three nodes. This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity observations, which independently show all three boot_ids changed (node1: ebd78841->bad09383, node2: c207ab79->ce84b78f, node3: d6298ced->92f673f7) and post-restart listening-sockets/package-health remained healthy with no failed services.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied: node1 was configured with PowerDNS Recursor to authoritatively answer inventory.internal with node2's private address (10.100.11.11) and forward all other queries to upstream resolvers (1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9), and node2/node3 were reconfigured via nmcli to use node1 as their DNS server, with resolution of both internal and external names verified from both nodes. The independently required provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated on all three nodes, with pre-restart baselines, reboot acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot identities, and confirmed recovery of DNS service and resolution, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is high; the only residue is a trivial /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the reboot mechanism on two nodes.
limitations: The lifecycle collector's after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so no independent pre/post-prepare comparison was possible beyond what the executor itself captured.

Evidence for external upstream resolution relies on public domains (google.com) rather than a fully isolated test of upstream-only forwarding behavior, but this is a reasonable and sufficient proxy for the requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's non-final commands were almost entirely read-only discovery (find, cat, grep, sed on VyOS template/conf_mode files) to determine the correct DNS-forwarding schema before committing config; none of these mutated state. The state-changing commands (VyOS set/commit/save on node1, nmcli con mod/con up on node2 and node3, and the three sequential native reboots) each map directly to a material task outcome or the mandatory restart protocol; no unnecessary or unreverted troubleshooting mutations were found. The one minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log left behind on node2 and node3 by the nohup-backgrounded reboot invocation, a small, inert, non-security-relevant artifact from the required restart mechanism rather than an independent mutation, so it is treated as low-severity leftover rather than a penalized unnecessary change.
